name: go-app-named-outlets-and-teleported-ui-subtrees
instr:
Add named outlets so applications can render UI elsewhere in the physical tree while preserving its logical ancestry, lifecycle, and addressability. Callers declare destinations with `Outlet(name, body...)` and contributors with `Teleport(outlet, body...)`, using the public `OutletName` type. The capability must behave consistently in browser rendering, server output, HTTP delivery, static generation, and public inspection.

Each non-empty outlet name identifies at most one destination, and invalid or duplicate declarations fail atomically with an `OutletError` that identifies the name and conflicting logical locations. Teleported text, raw, HTML, and component values retain representation semantics and logical parentage while selector expansion preserves deterministic declaration order. Events and dispatch follow logical component ancestors exactly once in parent-before-child order, never scheduling a physical host merely because it contains relocated content. Reconciliation keeps every current contributor exactly once, reorders unchanged components without remounting them, and releases lifecycle resources and handlers exactly once when either side disappears. `MissingOutletPolicy` provides `MissingOutletError`, `MissingOutletInline`, and `MissingOutletOmit`; every consumer applies the selected outcome identically, and omissions appear in the `PlacementReport`. Browser and server resolution produce equivalent placements and ordering, while Handler responses and static pages
